manifest.name: dsh-free-web
manifest.description: 免费联网搜索：不用搜索 API，抓取 Bing 公开结果页，必要时用本机 Chrome/Edge 无头渲染；为内置 web_search 提供搜索能力，并在输入框加入「关闭 / 智能 / 始终」三档联网开关、在左侧栏加入搜索面板。
manifest.author: dsh-free-web contributors

bundle.text:
# Bundle patch layer for dsh-free-web.
#
# 1. Insert the Host half. The same row id (`free-web`) is the web-search
#    provider id this plugin registers into `ctx.web`.
# 2. Point the shipped `web` service at that provider, so the built-in
#    `web_search` tool runs through the free engine instead of a search API.
#    `config` replaces the row's config wholesale, so restate every field the
#    shipped row sets: `fetchProvider: http` keeps the existing (API-free) HTTP
#    fetcher selected, otherwise the two fetch providers become ambiguous and
#    `web_fetch` fails.
- insert:
    - id: free-web
      name: dsh-free-web
- id: web
  name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-web'
  config:
    searchProvider: free-web
    fetchProvider: http

readme.text: Free web search for [DeepSeek Harness](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness) (DSH) with **no search API and no API key**.

`dsh-free-web` registers a search provider that reads Bing's public result page over plain HTTPS, falls back to its RSS view, and only then falls back to a local Chrome/Edge headless render. It powers DSH's built-in `web_search` tool, adds a per-session **Web off / Smart / Always** toggle next to the composer's permission control, and adds a search panel to the left sidebar.

No browser extension is involved. DSH's UI is a web surface, so this package has two halves: a Host half (Node) and a Client half (React components loaded by DSH itself). Chrome is only an optional headless renderer invoked by the Host.

[中文说明](README.zh.md)

- **No search API, no key**: the provider scrapes the same public result page a browser would load.
- **Three search modes per session** in the composer toolbar:
  - **Off** — `web_search` is blocked by a Host guard; `web_fetch` stays available for links the user provides.
  - **Smart** (default) — the model decides during reasoning when to search, and may search repeatedly and follow up with `web_fetch`.
  - **Always** — the Host runs one search automatically at the start of every user turn, injects the results as runtime context, and the model may search again if they are insufficient.
- **Left-sidebar panel** for manual searches, with engine status and per-result links.
- **Works on Web and Desktop**: routes live under `/api/dsh-free-web/` and the Client half uses relative URLs, so the same code works for `dsh web` and the Desktop shell's `dsh-app://` page.
- **Fail-open**: if every engine fails, the agent tool falls back to its normal error and the turn continues.

The composer toggle — pick **Off / Smart / Always** for the current session:

The sidebar panel — engine status, manual search, and per-result links:

- DSH **0.2.1-rc.3** or newer (developed and tested against 0.2.1-rc.3, `desktop` profile, Windows 11).
- Node.js 20+ on the Host (DSH bundles its own runtime).
- Optional: Google Chrome or Microsoft Edge for the render fallback. It is auto-detected; the plugin also works with HTTP-only search.

Clone the repository somewhere stable (the profile links to this directory, so do not delete it):

```bash
git clone https://github.com/skyhome000/dsh-free-web.git
```

Then install it as a local DSH bundle, either from the GUI (**Plugins → Add plugin → from directory**) or with the plugin-manager tool:

```text
plugin_manager install_bundle target: /absolute/path/to/dsh-free-web
```

Refresh the DSH window once (`Ctrl+R`) after installing or updating, so the browser half is loaded.

The bundle patch switches the built-in `web` service to this provider and keeps the existing HTTP fetcher selected:

```yaml
- id: web
  name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-web'
  config:
    searchProvider: free-web

Uninstalling the bundle removes the patch and restores the shipped defaults.
The button sits to the right of the permission preset in the composer toolbar and shows the current mode (`🌐 Smart web`):

| Mode | Behaviour |
| --- | --- |
| **Web off** | `web_search` calls are rejected by a Host guard; `web_fetch` remains available so the model can open a URL the user supplied. |
| **Smart** (default) | The model searches on its own when the answer needs current or externally verifiable facts, and may search several times while reasoning. |
| **Always** | The Host automatically runs one search for the turn before the first model step (15 s cap) and injects the results as runtime context; the model uses them and can refine with more searches. |
The mode is stored per session in `%DSH_HOME%/free-web/session-modes.json` (up to 500 sessions) and applies to the next step immediately — no new session needed.

| Setting | Value |
| --- | --- |
| `DSH_FREE_WEB_CHROME` / `CHROME_PATH` | Explicit browser executable path. |
| Auto-detected paths | Chrome and Edge under Program Files / Program Files (x86) / LocalAppData on Windows; `/Applications/Google Chrome.app/…`, `/usr/bin/google-chrome`, `chromium`, `microsoft-edge` elsewhere. |
| Results | `web_search` asks for up to 8 sources; the panel requests 8. |
| Timeouts | HTTP page 7 s, RSS 6 s, local browser 22 s, panel request 40 s, automatic search 15 s. |
| Mode store | `%DSH_HOME%/free-web/session-modes.json`. |
There is no plugin `Config` schema; the values above are code constants and environment variables.

- Routes accept only local callers: a missing `Origin`, `null`, the `dsh-app:` shell origin, or a loopback host (`127.0.0.1`, `localhost`, `[::1]`). Other origins get `403`.
- `POST` must be `application/json`, which is the CSRF boundary: a cross-site JSON request needs a preflight that only local origins pass. Bodies are capped at 64 KiB; queries at 400 characters.
- No cookies, no browser session, no login state is read. The optional headless browser starts with a fresh temporary profile and is deleted afterwards.
- Search results are external, untrusted data. The built-in `web_search` tool already labels them as untrusted; the panel does the same.

```bash
npm test        # node:test — 15 offline unit tests
npm run check   # node --check for both halves
```

The tests cover the HTML/RSS parsers (including Bing redirect unwrapping), the route/guard wiring, the per-session mode route, and the Client half's slot registrations and toggle rendering. They use a temporary `DSH_HOME` and never touch the network.

```text
index.js              Host half: provider, routes, mode store, agent policy
client.js             Client half: sidebar panel and composer toggle
cordis.patch.yml      Bundle patch: plugin row + web.searchProvider override
locale/{en,zh}.json   Plugin title/description for the Plugin Manager

- Bing can change its markup, rate-limit scraping, or serve different results by region; the chain retries through RSS and a local browser, but relevance is Bing's.
- In **Always** mode the automatic query is the user's message text (up to 400 characters). Long or conversational prompts may produce broad results; the model is instructed to refine with its own search.
- The Chrome fallback is slower (typically 6–15 s) and is only used when HTTP parsing fails.
